chunks: From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who goes along with a Muslim to help him in his need and counsels him sincerely in it, Allah will write for him, for every step, a good deed and erase from him a misdeed, whether the need is fulfilled or not. If he does not counsel him sincerely, then he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be his opponent.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a Muslim with their needs according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* underscores the spiritual weight of *nasihah* (sincere counsel) in fulfilling the rights of believers, linking physical effort to divine accounting. It highlights that the merit is secured by the intention and sincerity of the helper, irrespective of whether the request is ultimately granted, while framing insincerity as a breach of covenant with Allah and the Prophet. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the internal state (*ikhlas*) accompanying external acts of service.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 107. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:

One who goes along with a Muslim to help him and counsels him accordingly, Allah will write for him, for every step (he takes), a good deed and erases from him a misdeed regardless of whether he succeeds in helping him or not. If he does not counsel him sincerely, then he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger, and it is the Messenger of Allah (a.s) who will litigate against him.
